idiom_name: one commit boundary: enlist the queue, or defer the send to commit
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: open the business transaction, perform the state change, and either stage the send in a queue that is a participant of the same transaction (transacted session, transactional queue/topic, XA resource) or write the message into an outbox row inside that same transaction and publish it from the commit boundary. Choose enlistment when the queue is a resource manager and the deployment already runs a transaction coordinator; choose deferral when it is not, at the cost of a relay and at-least-once publication. Whichever way, publication must not happen before the commit decision, the unit of work must stay short, and the consumer must be idempotent because duplicates survive the pattern.
code_sketch:
begin_transaction()
  write_business_state()          # database / domain store
  stage_send(queue, message)      # invisible to consumers until commit
commit_transaction()              # both become visible, or neither does
# without a transactional queue:
begin_transaction(); write_business_state(); insert_outbox(message); commit()
publish_committed_outbox_rows()   # relay, at-least-once, delete only after ack
pitfalls: Publishing before the commit decision (inside the transaction body) recreates the phantom-message bug while looking transactional.
Stretching one transaction across services or a WAN instead of compensating with a process manager.
Assuming exactly-once delivery: the receiver still needs idempotency and, in a stream, offset commits inside the same transaction.
Leaving the transaction open across business calls or user interaction, so locks and broker timeouts dominate the failure profile.

Wrong move: treating a broker acknowledgement (a RabbitMQ publisher confirm, or tx.commit on a RabbitMQ channel) as atomic with the business transaction -> the ack only orders the message inside the broker, so the database work can still roll back after the send was confirmed -> instead use an outbox row in the local database transaction; RabbitMQ itself steers users to publisher confirms over channel transactions, which are synchronous and throughput-heavy and never cover the database anyway.

Wrong move: producing transactionally but leaving consumers of the topic on isolation.level=read_uncommitted -> consumers act on records from a transaction that later aborts, reintroducing the phantom-message bug on the read side -> instead configure every consumer of a transactional topic with isolation.level=read_committed (KIP-98).

Wrong move: opening a cross-entity Azure Service Bus transaction with an operation on an arbitrary entity -> the first operation fixes the transaction's routing path, so subsequent operations on other entities fail with InvalidOperationException -> instead sequence the operations so the routing entity is touched first, or route all entities through a send-via transfer.
